examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Reusing an earlier expression requires the same operator and operand values still available. Any intervening redefinition of an operand kills that expression's availability. Available-expression analysis is forward and must: a value is available at a join only if computed on every incoming path without a kill. Aliasing, volatile accesses, exceptions and function side effects can block transformations that look algebraically valid.

**Key relationship:** Available IN at a join = intersection of predecessor OUT sets

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify expression and operand definitions.
2. Check every incoming path for computation and kills.
3. Preserve aliasing and side-effect semantics.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: An expression is available only if it has been evaluated on every incoming path and none of its operand variables changed since. This is a forward must-analysis, so path merges intersect available sets. Identical text alone is insufficient when an intervening assignment kills the expression.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
x=a+b; a=a+1; y=a+b; z=a+b. Assuming no side effects, how many of the three a+b evaluations are redundant?

**Answer: 1.** The first computes the old a+b. Updating a invalidates it, so y's evaluation is necessary. No operand changes before z, making only z's evaluation redundant; it can reuse y.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Saving an expression in a variable that is later overwritten may require a new temporary even if the expression remains mathematically available.

Matching expression text is insufficient when operands or referenced memory may have changed.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

t=a+b; a=7; u=a+b. Can u always reuse t?

- **A.** Always if b is positive
- **B.** Yes
- **C.** No, a was redefined
- **D.** Only because addition is commutative

**Answer: C.** The second expression may use a different a. Redefining an operand kills availability of the earlier value.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Available-expression analysis is forward
- **B.** Must-availability intersects predecessor facts
- **C.** A write to an operand may kill availability
- **D.** Matching source text always guarantees equal values

**Answer: A, B, C.** Operand values may change while textual expressions remain identical, so D is false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

t1=a+b; t2=a+b; t3=t1*t2, with immutable a,b. Minimum additions after common-subexpression reuse?



**Answer: 1.** Compute a+b once and reuse the result for t2. The multiplication remains separate.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2026 CS1 · Q42 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/common-subexpressions?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Common subexpression elimination. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. g*k is computed on both incoming paths to B4 and neither g nor k changes. It is therefore available at B4 and redundant there.
2. b+i was computed in B1, but B3 assigns b=c+m, killing that expression on one path. It is not available on every path.
3. c+m is computed only along B3, so it is not redundant at B5, which is also reached via B2. Answer: **B4 {g*k}, B5 empty, D**.
